title: Alignment through Meta-Weighted Online Sampling: Bridging the Gap between Data Generation and Preference Optimization
claim: A learned meta-module couples sample generation with training by adaptively choosing and weighting data, yielding higher performance at lower generation and annotation cost.
layout: 2 panels: left two-tier flow (generation on top, training below) with a central meta-learner and curved feedback arrows; right dual-axis line and bar chart over three iterations
description: The left panel is a cartoon-style pipeline on two tinted bands: a blue Generation band on top and a pink Training band below. In the top band, an offline dataset icon flows via an 'Adaptive Sample' arrow to an LLM robot, then via 'Generate' to a response bubble. In the bottom band, offline and online data combine and flow through 'Weighted Train' to an updated LLM robot. A brain icon labeled Meta-Learner sits in the middle, linked to both bands by curved orange and blue arrows. The right panel is a dual-axis chart over Iter 1 to Iter 3. Lines show AlpacaEval 2 win rate for Online DPO, SELM and MetaAPO, with MetaAPO highest. Hatched bars show generation and annotation ratio, with MetaAPO lowest. The eye goes first to the colorful robots and the brain.
caption: Left: Overview of \model. MetaAPO employs a meta-learner to couple online data generation (top) and model training (bottom). The meta-learner adaptively assigns weights by evaluating offline data, guiding both targeted online sample generation and training on the weighted combination of offline and online samples. Right: Performance (left y-axis, line plots) and online generation and annotation ratio relative to Online DPO (right y-axis, bar plots) across training iterations for different methods.
abstract: Preference optimization is crucial for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values and intentions. A significant challenge in this process is the distribution mismatch between pre-collected offline preference data and the evolving model policy. Existing methods attempt to reduce this gap using static heuristics or decoupled online sampling strategies, but they often fail to adapt to the model's dynamic learning state. To bridge this gap, we propose Meta-Weighted Adaptive Preference Optimization (MetaAPO), a novel framework that dynamically couples data generation with model training. MetaAPO employs a lightweight meta-learner, as an "alignment gap estimator", to evaluate the potential benefits of on-policy sampling in relation to offline data. This guides targeted online generation and assigns sample-wise meta-weights to the optimization objective, dynamically balancing the quality and distribution of online and offline data. Experiments on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard and MT-Bench demonstrate that MetaAPO consistently outperforms existing preference optimization approaches across various settings, while reducing 42% in online annotation costs. Code is available at https://github.com/junming-yang/MetaAPO.
